module_mood_contract: Joyful creation — "it works, on my repo" (M1 closer lecture; sits after compound-and-close (Ex3), before the Bridge to M2)
cycle_close_re_fire_note: Re-fire under amended rules, prior verdict was REVISE (2 blocking: §1 mood floor at 6/10, §4 front-run). Body is unchanged; three things now exist that didn't when the prior verdict ran: check_writing.md #11 carries a carve-out for deliberate reinforcement of a fundamental (test = does the second mention do different work, not is it the second mention); check_pedagogy.md §14 excludes orientation (naming neighbouring stages to locate a lived one) from its black-box concern; and the strategy doc's M1 section (~line 278) plus this file's own maintainer block now both state the Klaassen double-naming across compound-and-close.md and this file is deliberate spaced repetition, not drift. This verdict independently re-examined both prior blocking findings against that new material rather than deferring to it. Conclusion: partial agreement, not full agreement -- see rule_index 1 and 4 evidence, and teaching_moment_lands below, for exactly which part of the maintainer's reasoning holds and which part doesn't.
teaching_moment_lands: Substantially resolved to PASS, with one residual, non-blocking defect the rule change does not touch. Named teaching moment: naming 'compound engineering' onto the four-move loop (orient/fix/compound/close) the student just ran -- a recognition beat, not a first teaching. Clause-by-clause re-read of the closer's Klaassen sentence (L43), applying check_writing.md #11's own test ('not is this the second mention, but does the second do different work') to each clause rather than to the paragraph as a whole: (1) 'The pattern has a name. Kieran Klaassen at Every calls it **compound engineering**.' -- clears the test. Verified against compound-and-close.md's current student-facing body (its 'The point:' line, L9): that file names Klaassen and prints his eight-stage loop, but the two-word coined term 'compound engineering' never appears in its student-facing text. The closer is the first place the student reads that label. Credit-at-point-of-use (Ex3) and name-the-thing-at-the-close (here) genuinely are different jobs on this clause, exactly as the strategy doc and maintainer block argue. This resolves the largest part of the prior finding -- 'The pattern has a name' is not, as previously judged, an entirely spent reveal. (2) 'The retro you just ran was the compound step of his loop: ideate -> brainstorm -> plan -> work -> review -> polish -> compound -> repeat.' -- does NOT clear the test. This is the identical correspondence claim (retro = his compound stage) and the identical eight-word chain compound-and-close.md's 'The point:' line already gave the student twenty minutes earlier; nothing in this clause does a job the first placement didn't already do. A one-clause callback ('the retro you just ran was that loop's compound step') would carry the same payload without the verbatim reprint. (3) 'That is the orient, fix, compound, close loop cut at different joints; the names differ, the loop doesn't.' -- new content (the strategy doc doesn't make this specific 4-vs-8 mapping claim anywhere), but underargued: the sentence asserts loop-equivalence directly beside a step count that visibly doubled (4 vs. 8), anchored by exactly one shown correspondence (retro=compound, step seven of eight), with no indication of where the other three student moves (orient, fix, close) sit inside Klaassen's other seven stages. 'Cut at different joints' would be the right frame for a granularity change; 'the names differ' claims something narrower and, on the sentence's own evidence, not fully shown. This defect is NOT addressed by any of the three amended-rule surfaces (check_writing #11 is about attribution-cap, not argument quality; check_pedagogy §14's orientation carve-out is about unexplained nouns not being invocations, not about whether a stated equivalence is earned; the strategy doc's new paragraph defends WHY naming twice is fine, not whether the mapping claim holds). Fragility check per the story template ('if the persona could skip it, the artefact is fragile'): the persona can skip this one clause and still get the core recognition ('this has a name, and I did it') -- the beat's central function survives a reader's skepticism about this one sub-claim, which is why this is recorded as a flagged, non-blocking TODO rather than a blocking failure, distinct from clause (2)'s cost, which is recorded under rule_index 1's mood scoring below.
maintainer_reasoning_assessment: The maintainer block states two things will re-flag this closer and 'both are wrong': a judge reading either file alone, and a persona sim scoring the beat as a spent reveal because it 'measures novelty where the design wants recall.' Independently checked both. The first is correct as stated -- this judge now reads both files together and confirms the coined-term reveal is real, not spent. The second is overstated. 'Measures novelty' is not the right diagnosis of what the residual mood cost is: spaced repetition as a retention mechanism works through retrieval or reframing, and this beat does neither for clause (2) above -- it restates an already-established correspondence and an already-printed chain verbatim, which reads as flat repetition to an attentive reader independent of whether the reader is 'looking for novelty.' A persona who already trusts the retro=compound mapping (given, correctly, in Ex3) gains nothing from seeing the same clause and the same eight-word chain a second time; genuine spaced repetition would ask the student to supply the mapping themselves, or would shorten the callback so the new material (the term, the broader claim) carries the sentence instead of restating the old material alongside it. So: the maintainer's ruling to keep the closer's double-naming stands and is right on its own terms (the term-reveal clause earns its place); the specific claim that a low score is purely a novelty-measurement artifact does not fully hold, because part of the cost is genuine textual redundancy the rule change didn't address. Net effect on verdict: this is not laundered into a clean PASS -- it is scored as facilitator-premium (7/10, not 8), which keeps the finding visible as a TODO rather than either re-blocking the file or erasing the concern.
